"'''Can't Get Used to Losing You'''" is a song written by [[Doc Pomus|Jerome "Doc" Pomus]] and [[Mort Shuman]], first made popular by [[Andy Williams]] in a 1963 record release, which was a number-two hit in both the US and the UK.  Twenty years later, British band [[The Beat (British band)|The Beat]] took a [[reggae]] re-arrangement to number three in the UK.

"Can't Get Used to Losing You" is a song written by Jerome "Doc" Pomus and Mort Shuman, first made popular by Andy Williams in a 1963 record release, which was a number-two hit in both the US and the UK.  Twenty years later, British band The Beat took a reggae re-arrangement to number three in the UK.

sections.heading: Andy Williams recording
sections.wikitext:
"Can't Get Used to Losing You" was recorded by Andy Williams in December 1962 and released in 1963. It peaked at number two in both the US and the UK.  In the US, the single spent four weeks at number two on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart (behind "[[He's So Fine]]" by [[the Chiffons]] and "[[I Will Follow Him]]" by [[Peggy March|Little Peggy March]]) and topped the [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Easy Listening chart]] for four weeks, peaking on both in April 1963.<ref>[[Joel Whitburn|Whitburn, Joel]] (1996). ''The Billboard Book of Top 40 Hits'', 6th Edition (Billboard Publications)</ref>  Williams' recording peaked at number one on the ''[[Cashbox (magazine)|Cashbox]]'' charts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.popularsong.org/tidbits25.html|title=PopularSong.org, "Meet the Boxes, Juke and Cash"}}</ref> 

Williams' vocals on the song's verses were double-tracked in unison, and overdubbed on the choruses so the listener hears Williams singing harmony with himself.{{citation needed|date=April 2023}} The song appears on an album titled ''[[Days of Wine and Roses and Other TV Requests]]'' in North America and ''Can't Get Used to Losing You and Other Requests'' in the United Kingdom.

sections.heading: Other 1960s covers
sections.wikitext: In 1963, [[Patti Page]] recorded a version, with strings background, as part of the ''[[Say Wonderful Things (album)|Say Wonderful Things]]'' album.  In the same year, [[Paul Anka]] included it on the album ''Song I Wish I'd Written'', and Julie London performed it on ''[[The Wonderful World of Julie London]].'' In 1965, [[Chad and Jeremy]]'s cover appeared on their ''[[Before and After (Chad & Jeremy album)|Before and After]].'' Welsh band [[Amen Corner (band)|Amen Corner]] covered the song on their debut album ''Round Amen Corner''.{{citation needed|date=October 2026}}

[[The Beat (British band)|The Beat]] (known as The English Beat in the USA) originally recorded their cover of "Can't Get Used to Losing You" as a track on their 1980 album ''[[I Just Can't Stop It]]''.  It was not released as a single until three years later, just as the Beat announced that they were breaking up.  The single was remixed slightly from the album track, and became the band's fifth and final top ten UK hit, and their highest-charting single release.

[[Elvis Costello]], who singled out the song as his favorite Doc Pomus composition, had hoped to cover the song, but scrapped the idea after "the Beat beat me to it".<ref>{{Cite book |last=Costello |first=Elvis |title=Unfaithful music & disappearing ink |date=2015 |publisher=Blue Rider Press |isbn=978-0-399-16725-6 |location=New York}}</ref>
